Subject: HealthSync trial environment checkpoints & recommended next steps

Emma — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a concrete set of checkpoints so we can get the trial moving without surprises. If anything below is off, flag it and we’ll adjust.

1) Recap of objectives (what we agreed on)
- Validate retrieval + LLM response quality for clinical note summarization and question-answering over patient records (PHI redaction will be in scope).
- Measure latency and cost at sample throughput (target is interactive product usage).
- Verify that the model pipeline integrates with your S3 store and search index.

2) Success criteria (proposal)
- Functional: summaries match current human baseline >85% accuracy on curated eval set; QA F1 >0.78 on sampled prompts.
- Performance: p95 inference latency <= 350ms for 512-token queries (hosted path), sustained 6 QPS throughputs for peak scenarios.
- Economics: end-to-end token cost benchmarked so projected cost per 1k tokens <= internal threshold (we’ll estimate after first 48h).
- Security/compliance: SOC2 audit evidence & audit-logging enabled; for PHI flows we need either VPC or encrypted-hosted agreement.

3) High-level evaluation plan
- Week 0 (prep): exchange sample dataset manifest, grant temporary read-only S3 access to sample bucket, share security contact.
- Week 1–2 (hosted baseline): ingest sample data, prompt tuning, capture baseline metrics and qualitative review with your SMEs.
- Week 3 (scale/variant test): run dedicated sandbox or VPC trial for larger batch runs and integration tests; compare results and cost.

4) Environment options (short pros/cons)
- Hosted API (fastest onboarding): no infra changes on your side, best for quick prompt tuning and early quality checks.
  - Pros: <48h to get started, streaming, built-in metrics.
  - Cons: not ideal for long-term PHI unless covered by contractual terms; egress controls limited to platform policies.
- Dedicated sandbox (reserved capacity in our infra): predictable throughput, isolated tenancy, quicker to provision than VPC but still managed by Redwood.
  - Pros: consistent latency, easier benchmarking.
  - Cons: requires billing commit; ~3–5 business days to provision.
- VPC trial (VPC peering / Private deployment): best for PHI/regulatory environments, full network control.
  - Pros: data stays in customer-controlled network, KMS integrations, full audit logs.
  - Cons: setup 7–14 business days for initial connectivity and certificate exchange.

Recommendation: start with a 10–14 day hosted baseline to validate quality and prompts, then run a parallel VPC connectivity setup so you can switch to an isolated path for PHI tests without redoing the eval. This minimizes time-to-insight while preserving a migration path.

5) Proposed timeline & owners (suggested)
- Tue 4/2: Technical kickoff (1h) — deliverables: S3 access + sample manifest — owner: Ben Carter (redwood); action: Emma to confirm attendees and procurement contact.
- Week of 4/8: Hosted baseline starts — owner: Ben (onboarding), Laura (success criteria reporting).
- Week of 4/22: Parallel VPC provisioning begins if needed — owner: Redwoods infra team (Ben lead), HealthSync security (Samir).
- Week of 5/6: Consolidated readout + decision to proceed to production path.

6) Asks from your side (please confirm)
- Procurement timeline / PO expectation (date).
- Security lead contact for questionnaire and certs (name + email).
- Sample data access (S3 path or manifest).
- Any network constraints (CIDR ranges / proxies) we should know up-front.

I attached a short trial playbook and our POC checklist for your review. If you’re aligned with the plan above I’ll propose times for the technical kickoff and loop in our infra engineer to start the VPC checklist in parallel.

Thanks — Jonas

Emma / Samir — quick follow-up with specifics on PHI handling and an initial VPC checklist so your security team can triage.

1) PHI handling on hosted baseline
- Hosted baseline: we do not perform persistent indexing of raw files beyond the trial evaluation window (default retention 30 days) unless you request longer. For PHI-sensitive records we recommend either: (a) pre-redact before ingestion, or (b) route PHI flows to the VPC path once connectivity is ready. We can enable stricter retention and automatic deletion hooks for trial buckets as an interim measure.

2) Initial VPC checklist (short)
- Customer to provide: list of allowed egress CIDRs, bastion IP (if needed), S3 endpoint or cross-account role ARN, public cert for mTLS (optional).
- Redwood to provide: peering instructions, sample terraform for routing, expected cert fingerprints, and staging IP ranges.
- Estimated lead time: 7–14 business days after CIDR & cert exchange; can shorten to ~5 business days if your network team can apply our quick ACL template immediately.

3) Concrete success metrics (refined)
- Latency: p95 <= 350ms for 512-token interactive queries (hosted) / dedicated target p95 <= 300ms.
- Throughput: baseline 6 QPS sustained; burst to 15 QPS for stress tests.
- Quality: human-evaluated summary accuracy >= 85% on provided eval set; embedding similarity ROC-AUC target > 0.9 for retrieval recall tests.

4) Owners & next steps (who does what)
- Ben Carter (Redwood): onboarding lead — responsible for dataset ingestion, initial tuning, and access.
- Laura Bennett (Redwood): metrics/reporting — will produce a weekly dashboard and the readout.
- Samir Patel (HealthSync): security/questions and cert ownership.
- Procurement (procurement@healthsync.com): finalize PO; we can provision dedicated sandbox after PO confirmation (3–5 business days).

5) Proposed short actions for the next 7 days
- Emma: confirm procurement owner and PO target date (you mentioned 4/20).
- Samir: share main security contact and whether we should plan for pre-redaction (Samir@healthsync?).
- Ben: will spin up a hosted baseline environment once S3 access is granted; I’ll share the onboarding checklist in a separate link.

I’m attaching a short VPC checklist text file (vpc-setup-checklist.md) to get your network team started. If this looks good, Ben and I can propose a 1-hour technical kickoff on Tue 4/2 (we have morning slots).

—Jonas
